\begin{figure*}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig_pdg_ansatz.pdf}
  \caption{Quantum dependence in a hardware-efficient VQE ansatz, criterion $q_0$. Each node is an operation
  as it executes, with the source line and loop iteration that created it, and both graphs place every node
  at the same position. (b)~The classical PDG treats the control of a CNOT as read only. It lacks the orange
  edges, so its slice of $q_0$ (shaded) keeps only the rotations of $q_0$ and misses the outlined
  dependences. (c)~The wire rule has these edges as quantum edges, and its slice is exactly the dependences
  of $q_0$. Entanglement closure would also add the purple rotations, which are not dependences. Graphs,
  slices and fidelities at $\ket{0\dots0}$ are computed by the study's code from the program shown.}
  \label{fig:ansatz}
\end{figure*}

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig_pdg_teleport.pdf}
  \caption{Control dependence in teleportation, criterion $q_2$. The corrections depend on the measurements
  only through the green control edges. Def-use ignores classical bits, so its graph is this one without
  them, and its slice of $q_2$ misses the outlined operations. $F$ is the fidelity of $q_2$ at
  $\ket{0\dots0}$. Line comments are omitted from the code.}
  \label{fig:teleport}
\end{figure}
